newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit rises on commercial dollar sales.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit rises on commercial dollar sales.

text.p: * Ringgit rises on heavy commercial selling around 2.5140
* Stop-loss selling at 2.5100 by interbank players caught long on dollar
* Ringgit seen in new trading range of 2.5050-2.5150 a dollar
The ringgit rose against the dollar late Thursday morning on heavy commercial dollar sales, dealers said.
"The dollar sales started around 2.5140 and continued all the way down to about 2.5080," said a European bank dealer in Singapore.
The selling was believed to be part of the continued conversion of funds raised by an oil company from a dollar Eurobond issue, dealers said.
The sudden rise in the ringgit also triggered stop-loss dollar sales around 2.5100, they said.
"A lot of interbank players were caught long dollar and were unwinding their positions," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.

But downside for the dollar/ringgit was likely to be limited by the dollar's strength against the yen, dealers said, adding that they expected the dollar/ringgit to trade in a new range of 2.5050-2.5150.
At 0320 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5095/5105 a dollar against 2.5148/53 at Kuala Lumpur close on Wednesday.
